mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants anticipate accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines from t-2mo to t-1mo over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A labor market overheating condition defined by UNRATE below 4.0% and PAYEMS growth exceeding 0.5% monthly signals tight labor conditions that accelerate wage inflation and corporate cost pressures, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0 and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% (mo/mo) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in HOUST (housing starts) and increase in CPIAUCSL (inflation) signals weakening consumer demand and rising price pressures, triggering negative equity market reactions over the next 20 days due to profit margin compression.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where HOUST declines and CPIAUCSL rises (t-2mo to t-1mo) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A supply contraction signaled by INDPRO below 100 indicates manufacturing slowdown, reducing corporate output and earnings growth, which generates negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO < 100 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1350.0 thousand units signals robust consumer spending and economic confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through improved corporate revenue outlooks.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST > 1350.0 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL > 320.0) triggers anticipated Federal Reserve rate hikes that increase discount rates for equity valuation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 320.0 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in RSAFS (retail sales) and rise in UNRATE (unemployment) signals deteriorating consumer spending and labor market weakness, triggering negative equity returns over the next 20 days through reduced corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decline and UNRATE rise (t-2mo to t-1mo)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS declines and UNRATE rises (t-2mo to t-1mo) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle labor market overheating (PAYEMS > 150,000 and UNRATE < 4.0%) fuels wage inflation that erodes corporate profit margins, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as recession risks materialize.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS > 150000 and UNRATE < 4.0 over a 3-year rolling window.
